technical_and_design_decisions: Leverage Spring for Apache Kafka 6.x as the base integration for all Kafka-related features, aligned with Spring Framework 6.0 Java 17+ requirements.

Use Spring's @ConfigurationProperties abstraction to implement global Kafka configuration defaults, with per-deployment overrides supported via Spring profiles, environment variables, and externalized configuration.
Align Kafka ACK configuration with native Kafka producer acks semantics (0,1,all) exposed directly via Spring configuration properties.

Implement async request-reply (bindRequestor/bindReplier) using Spring's core messaging abstractions (MessageChannel, MessagingTemplate) with Kafka as the underlying transport, using native Kafka reply-to headers for message correlation.
Leverage Spring Kafka's native batch processing capabilities for the batching feature, exposing batch size and batch timeout as configurable properties.
Use Spring Batch as the base integration for Sqoop job management, leveraging existing job orchestration infrastructure for stop and incremental load features.
Capture Sqoop logs by redirecting Sqoop process stdout/stderr to the application's SLF4J logger, with job/execution context added to log MDC for traceability.
Implement incremental Sqoop data loads using Sqoop's native --incremental mode, with last imported value tracking stored in a configurable metadata store (e.g., database table, properties file).
All new features will include unit tests (JUnit 5, Mockito) and integration tests using Testcontainers for Kafka and Sqoop to ensure CI compatibility.
All new configuration properties will include validation constraints (e.g., @Min, @Max, @Pattern) to prevent invalid configuration values at application startup.
assumptions: The existing codebase already has Spring for Apache Kafka and Spring Batch 6.x dependencies integrated, so no new core framework dependencies are required.
The CI environment has Docker support available to run Testcontainers for Kafka and Sqoop integration tests.
The existing application logging system is SLF4J-compatible (e.g., Logback, Log4j2) so redirected Sqoop logs will be captured and routed correctly.
Sqoop jobs are already orchestrated via Spring Batch jobs, so existing job management infrastructure can be reused for stop and incremental load features.
Target deployment environments support Java 17+, as required by Spring Framework 6.0.
The connected Kafka cluster is version 3.0 or higher, compatible with Spring for Apache Kafka 6.x.
The Sqoop version used is 1.4.7 or higher, which supports incremental import modes and job termination.
There are no existing conflicting Kafka or Sqoop configurations in the current codebase that would require refactoring before implementing new features.
The existing CI pipeline supports running JUnit integration tests and publishing test results.

activities.activity_description: Define the structure for global Kafka default configuration properties, document per-deployment override patterns using Spring profiles, environment variables, and externalized config, align with existing application configuration conventions.

Add @ConfigurationProperties for Kafka consumer and producer concurrency settings, wire properties into existing Spring Kafka listener container and producer factory configurations, add validation for concurrency values (positive integers), perform local testing.

Add @ConfigurationProperties for supported Kafka compression types (gzip, snappy, lz4, zstd, none), wire properties into Kafka producer and consumer configurations, add validation for allowed compression values, perform local testing.
Add @ConfigurationProperties for Kafka producer acks level (0, 1, all), wire property into Kafka producer configuration, add validation for allowed acks values, update configuration documentation.

Develop a Spring bean that binds a Kafka producer for async request-reply patterns, implement correlation ID handling, configurable request timeout, and reply topic header injection, use Spring MessagingTemplate for request sending and reply handling, add configuration properties for requestor settings.

Develop a Spring bean that binds a Kafka consumer to handle incoming request messages, implement async request processing, reply generation and sending to the reply-to topic specified in request headers, add configuration properties for replier settings.

Add @ConfigurationProperties for Kafka batch size and batch timeout settings, wire properties into Spring Kafka batch message listener container, add validation for batch configuration values, update documentation for batching usage.

Write integration tests using Testcontainers for Kafka to validate all new Kafka features (concurrency, compression, acks, request-reply, batching), configure tests to run in the CI pipeline, add test result reporting, ensure tests pass on every CI build.

Add @ConfigurationProperties to enable/disable Sqoop job stop on completion, implement logic using Spring Batch JobOperator to send stop signals to running Sqoop jobs, add error handling for failed stop operations, perform local testing.

activities.activity_description: Implement logic to capture Sqoop job stdout/stderr output, route logs to the application's SLF4J logger, add job/execution ID to log MDC for traceability, add configuration to enable/disable log streaming, test log capture and routing.

Add @ConfigurationProperties for Sqoop incremental load mode (append/lastmodified), incremental column name, and last value tracking, implement last imported value persistence in a configurable metadata store, wire properties into Sqoop job configuration, add validation for incremental load parameters, test both incremental modes.

Write integration tests using Testcontainers (or mock Sqoop environment) to validate Sqoop job stop, log capture, and incremental load functionality, configure tests to run in the CI pipeline, ensure all Sqoop-related user stories are covered by tests.
